holidays.name: National Sangria Day
holidays.description: Pour a big pitcher of wine, chopped fruit and a splash of something bubbly or boozy, and call it a holiday. It's a good way to bring some summery color to a winter party.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on the food and drink calendar.
holidays.funFact: The name comes from the Spanish word for blood, "sangre", a nod to the drink's deep red color.

holidays.name: National Fried Shrimp Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates shrimp dipped in batter or breadcrumbs and fried until golden and crunchy. Dunk them in cocktail sauce, pile them into a po' boy, or eat them straight from the basket.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is one of many days that honor a favorite comfort food.
holidays.funFact: Shrimp is one of the most popular seafoods in the United States, and fried shrimp is a staple of seafood shacks from the Gulf Coast to New England.

holidays.name: Go Caroling Day
holidays.description: Bundle up, gather some friends and belt out holiday songs for your neighbors. Off-key singing is allowed, and so are jingle bells and silly hats.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It builds on the old tradition of wandering groups singing seasonal songs door to door.
holidays.funFact: The word "carol" originally meant a circle dance accompanied by singing, not a song sung while standing still.
